top3.headline: Claude Code's product lead leaves Anthropic for OpenAI
top3.whyItMatters: The person who shipped Claude Code now shapes OpenAI's core products, including agents.

top3.headline: OpenAI vows to pay its own way on future compute campuses
top3.whyItMatters: After midterm backlash on data centers, OpenAI is writing the local deal terms itself.

top3.headline: Tencent's Hy4 adds vision and computer use at preview prices
top3.whyItMatters: Another lab ships CLI and GUI computer use, so agent desktop work is no longer a niche bet.

items.title: Intuit's CEO maps AI into accounting and mid-market ERP
items.takeaway: Goodarzi says earlier AI agents worked in slices but failed end-to-end; Intuit now builds system-level workflows.
items.soWhat: If accountants are the retention layer, AI that only answers questions will not keep mid-market customers.

items.title: Senate set to vote on technology-neutral permitting reform
items.takeaway: BAAJA could unlock hundreds of gigawatts of energy and transmission while also speeding natural-gas plants for AI load.
items.soWhat: Grid capacity for AI campuses now hinges on a November 9 Senate vote with post-midterm uncertainty.

items.title: Overalls slips weeks to run Antithesis verification on Firecracker
items.takeaway: Huntley is delaying overalls.dev while prototyping distributed builds and content-addressable cache on Firecracker.
items.soWhat: Self-hosted agent machines are being held to production reliability bars before public launch.

items.title: OpenAI publishes a National Community Compact for compute campuses
items.takeaway: Owned campuses will pay full electricity costs, publish water and energy use, limit official NDAs, and report hiring.
items.soWhat: Communities now have OpenAI's own checklist to demand when a campus comes to town.

image.alt: OpenAI Blog: OpenAI publishes a National Community Compact for compute campuses

items.title: Claude Code's product lead Cat Wu joins OpenAI for Core Products
items.takeaway: OpenAI confirmed Wu will work with Nick Turley and Ashley Alexander and report to Codex lead Thibault Sottiaux.
items.soWhat: OpenAI is buying Anthropic product talent just as Claude Code defined the agent coding category.

items.title: Nathan Benaich calls 'US SOTA' open-weight framing odd energy
items.takeaway: He argues crowning a model SOTA among American open weights while it trails Chinese open models is a weak win.
items.soWhat: Investors are judging open weights on a global ladder, not a US-only bracket.

items.title: SpecCompact drafts agent memory summaries with a small model first
items.takeaway: A small model drafts structured summary slots in parallel; a larger model verifies them to cut compaction latency.
items.soWhat: Long-running agents hit context limits; faster compaction is a direct cost and latency lever.

image.alt: arXiv: SpecCompact drafts agent memory summaries with a small model first

items.title: Paper tests turn-level best-of-N sampling for long-horizon agents
items.takeaway: At each turn a generator proposes N actions and a selector picks one for complex agent tasks.
items.soWhat: Teams can raise agent quality with more samples per step before training a bigger model.

image.alt: arXiv: Paper tests turn-level best-of-N sampling for long-horizon agents

items.title: CompressionBench asks coding agents to shrink model weights alone
items.takeaway: Agents get a checkpoint, storage limit, and time budget, then must keep pretrained behavior in smaller weights.
items.soWhat: If agents can compress models reliably, inference cost becomes an automated engineering loop.

image.alt: arXiv: CompressionBench asks coding agents to shrink model weights alone

items.title: ServerBench has agents design full LLM serving stacks for dollars
items.takeaway: The benchmark scores specialized serving systems on a dollars-per-dollar objective across latency and correctness.
items.soWhat: Serving infrastructure is becoming something agents can experiment on, not only humans.

image.alt: arXiv: ServerBench has agents design full LLM serving stacks for dollars

items.title: Ask HN maps today's agent stacks: Claude Code, Codex, OpenClaw
items.takeaway: A 354-point thread shows Claude IDE with Opus 5.5, Codex subs, cheap OpenRouter routes, and harnesses like Pi.
items.soWhat: Real agent stacks are consolidating around a few paid harnesses plus cheap overflow models.

image.alt: Hacker News: Ask HN maps today's agent stacks: Claude Code, Codex, OpenClaw

items.title: Tencent Hy4 ships vision plus CLI and GUI computer use
items.takeaway: API is live on Tencent Cloud and OpenRouter at preview prices; weights and a system card are planned.
items.soWhat: Computer-use agents now have another production API option besides the usual US labs.

image.alt: Tencent Hunyuan: Tencent Hy4 ships vision plus CLI and GUI computer use
